<section class="hero">
<div class="hero-copy">
<p class="eyebrow">Exploratory methods note · July 2026</p>
<h1>What do language models imply about taxable-income responses?</h1>
<p class="deck">Four models answer the same stylized tax question. Their outputs disagree—often because some adjust income while others copy the supplied baseline.</p>
<p class="boundary"><strong>Model outputs, not human elasticities.</strong> The exercise studies what LLMs say under a prompt; it does not identify how taxpayers behave.</p>

<section class="editorial-section finding" id="finding">
<div class="section-index">
<span>01</span>
<p>The finding</p>
</div>
<div class="section-body">
<p class="display-statement">The four models do not produce a common response distribution.</p>
<div class="finding-grid">
<p>Claude changes broad and taxable income in most responses. DeepSeek adjusts less often but usually moves in the direction implied by a positive response. Gemma and GPT-4o mini usually preserve the baseline, with occasional large or zero-dollar answers.</p>
<p>That mixture makes averages and medians tell different stories. A familiar-looking mean is therefore a property of the model, prompt, cleaning rule, and summary—not a validation against human behavior.</p>
</div>

<section class="editorial-section design" id="design">
<div class="section-index">
<span>02</span>
<p>The design</p>
</div>
<div class="section-body">
<p class="kicker">Every exclusion is visible.</p>
{{< include paper/generated/sample_flow.html >}}
<p class="method-note">The pipeline reconstructs the whole-dollar incomes and integer tax rates actually shown to each model. It removes duplicate delivered prompts and ambiguous reruns, estimates on a common panel, and reports model-specific and boundary sensitivities.</p>
<a class="inline-link" href="paper/#design-and-methods">Read the methods <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>
</div>
</section>

<section class="editorial-section interpretation" id="interpretation">
<div class="section-index">
<span>03</span>
<p>The boundary</p>
</div>
<div class="section-body two-column-statement">
<div>
<p class="kicker">What this can show</p>
<p>How model families encode a stylized tax question; where prompts and parsers create measurement choices; and whether model outputs remain stable across defensible summaries.</p>
</div>
<div>
<p class="kicker">What this cannot show</p>
<p>How people respond to tax reforms, whether an LLM can replace causal evidence, or what elasticity should be used to score a policy.</p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
